text.insert: Target-claim write sets, worker workspaces, integration validation, and shared artifact safety.

Write safety starts with category-typed target-claim write sets and isolated
worker workspaces. The state substrate records who owns a target, which approved
paths and categories that worker may touch, and whether a banked checkpoint is
tentative, confirmed, or regressed.

Before editing, a worker receives a target claim whose initial write set contains
the target source. The worker edits only approved paths. A necessary path outside
that set requires a handoff-note widening request with lower-rung evidence; an
unrequested path is categorized, recorded in telemetry, and returned as a repair
reason instead of being silently dropped or allowed to bank.

steps.text: create worker state with category-typed target-source write set

runner decides the request or returns categorized repair feedback
runner validates the touched compile blast and records a tentative checkpoint
integration follows the configured finish mode; the boundary confirms or regresses

text.insert:
| Rung | Category | Allowed Scope | Evidence Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | target-source | The target `.c`; type in-slice code to the existing foreign interface first. | Target compile and objdiff evidence. |
| 2 | config-metadata | The relevant `symbols.txt` or `splits.txt`. | The rung-1 failure, affected symbol or address range, and measured target result. |
| 3 | owning-header | The canonical header that owns the mismatched declaration or type. | Rung-1 and rung-2 failures, declaration-owner evidence, and measured target result. |
| 4 | foreign-source | The foreign `.c` that owns the definition. | Every lower-rung failure, definition-owner evidence, measured target result, and the affected-consumer scope. |

Widening requests travel through the worker handoff note. A request names one
category, its exact paths, the mismatched declaration or symbol, the expected
owner, objdiff evidence, and why each lower rung failed. The runner approves,
denies, defers, or routes it. Approval expands the live claim and returns a
continuation instruction; the other decisions return their reason and preserve
the best honest lower-rung result. Foreign-source requests remain routed for
cross-module handling rather than receiving automatic approval.

A recycled or re-picked-up target resets to the target-source entry. Its next
worker must re-earn config-metadata or owning-header widening with current
evidence. Historical requests and decisions remain available as telemetry but
do not carry authorization into the new claim.

The main checkout remains the canonical integration surface. Worker workspaces
are the normal execution surface. They isolate simultaneous attempts, allow
same-file targets to run concurrently, and keep unfinished source changes out
of the baseline until the runner selects a checkpoint.

Worker output integration is serial in both modes. With merge-on-finish off,
selected checkpoints wait in the integration queue. With it on, a checkpoint
that passes scoped checks is applied immediately into the current session
ancestry when the worker finishes. A clean application records a tentative
integration. A conflict invokes the conflict-resolver agent with both claims,
their evidence, and scoped-check results; an unresolved conflict falls back to
an operator-visible conflict state.

steps.text: merge-on-finish on: apply into session ancestry

Same-file and shared-support concurrency is expected to be rare but allowed.
Workers proceed in isolated workspaces; collisions are handled by serial
integration and the conflict-resolver agent rather than path locks that prevent
workers from starting.

The integration record carries checkpoint metadata, patch paths, category-typed
write sets, widening decisions, scoped-check evidence, conflict paths, target
identity, and validation state. The runner owns serial application and boundary
truth. The conflict-resolver agent edits only the supplied conflict group and
returns a resolved patch or an operator-visible conflict disposition.

Worker worktrees isolate source and build outputs, but the host still has a
finite amount of CPU, disk, and MWCC runner capacity. The runner therefore uses
slot pools for expensive local operations instead of letting every active
worker invoke them at once.

Runner-owned Ninja validation acquires an epoch-scoped worker Ninja slot before
running
in a worker worktree. Toolpack API calls such as

acquire a
tool-specific slot before launching their helper command. Slot directories live
beside the epoch worker worktrees, include an

with the owning PID,
and are pruned when stale.

These pools do not weaken write isolation: each command still runs against the
claim's own worktree and approved, category-typed write set. They only cap
concurrent compiler/tool pressure so a large worker pool keeps making progress
without turning every validation boundary into a machine-wide stampede.

Compile checks follow the touched set. Target-source and foreign-source edits
rebuild and compare their units; an owning-header edit adds its owner and direct
includers; config metadata adds units whose address ranges are affected and
compares their section measures. A passing improvement banks and integrates as
tentative. The epoch boundary runs the global build and zero-regression report:
a clean result confirms the tentative window, while a regression triggers blame
attribution, reverts the guilty change, marks it regressed, and confirms the
clean remainder.

| Risk | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Two workers edit the same file | Allow concurrent isolated workspaces; integrate selected checkpoints serially and route collisions through the conflict-resolver agent. |
| Header/data owner edits | Climb the four-rung necessity ladder, require lower-rung and owner evidence, and expand compile checks with the touched set. |
| Unrequested out-of-set edits | Categorize the paths, record telemetry, and issue a repair reason; never bank a silently narrowed patch. |
| Stale patch base | Score integration checks

; stale patches are rebased, revalidated, or rejected. |
| Shared build/tool pressure | Use worker-local worktrees plus epoch-scoped Ninja and tool slot pools; tune pool sizes before raising the worker count. |
| Shared CSV/artifact races | Workers write shards; reducers own shared summaries, charts, and merged artifacts. |
| Bad integration | Bank scoped-check passes as tentative; confirm them only at a clean boundary, or attribute, revert, and mark the guilty change regressed. |
